text:
nina: FYI ran into a nasty auth behavior with the python SDK in a long-running sidecar. Two clients, different API keys (via env), rotate the env at runtime and the first client never picks up the new key.
liam: can you share a minimal repro? sync or async?
nina: async. stripped down:

```
os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'] = 'alpha'
client_a = AsyncRedwoodClient()
# later, credentials rotated by external process
os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'] = 'bravo'
# client_a still authenticates as alpha
await client_a.chat.create(...)
```

priyanka: is the key passed to the constructor anywhere? if you pass api_key explicitly it should be pinned to that client.
nina: we rely on env for our sidecar. also tried calling client_a._refresh_credentials() (internal) and client still sent alpha.
liam: this screams global provider cache or singleton. might be cached at import/first-resolve.
jesse: interestingly, creating a new client after rotation picks up bravo most of the time, but timing affects it. racey.
priyanka: that pattern matters for customers running credential refresh daemons. we should document or change behavior. per-call env reads cost a bit but necessary for refresh use cases.
infra-bot: Created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/issues/857 (labels: bug, auth, regression)
liam: proposed quick fixes:
- allow AsyncRedwoodClient(api_key_provider=Callable[[],str]) so callers can inject dynamic provider
- add env_read_strategy param defaulting to cached but opt-in per_call
- expose a public refresh() method that forces provider reload

priyanka: +1 on typed provider interface (Protocol) so mypy users can rely on signatures. also add doc examples showing a lightweight provider that reads os.getenv each call.
jesse: for SDK team: add an integration test that spins two clients with different env values in same process and asserts requests contain respective auth headers over time. Also test concurrent init.
liam: perf tradeoff: per-call getenv vs cached. we should measure. add benchmark in CI perf-suite.
nina: workaround I used:

```
class EnvApiKeyProvider:
    def get(self):
        return os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')

client_a = AsyncRedwoodClient(api_key_provider=EnvApiKeyProvider())
```

priyanka: we should add a small snippet like that to the SDK-auth docs under "Long-running processes & key rotation".
jesse: tagging eng-sdks: @eng-sdks please prioritize medium and route to a single owner.
infra-bot: Routing to #eng-sdks (ticket: SDK-857)
liam: I'll draft a small PR that introduces an AuthProvider Protocol, optional api_key_provider param, and env_read_strategy flag. Keep cached default to preserve perf for most users.
nina: thanks all. saving this thread so other teams running sidecars don't waste hours. :coffee:
